title: Run of the marker-existence scanner
statement: Let $x$ and $r$ be Boolean words. For every word $p$ such that $x=pr$, there is a time $t\le |r|+1$ at which the marker-existence scanner, started on input $x$ in its initial state, with its input head positioned just after the prefix $p$ and with empty output, is halted and has output the one-bit word that is true exactly when $r$ contains a true bit.
hypotheses_covered: The starting scan configuration uses state $()$, position $|p|$, and empty output
replaced:
For any split $x = p s$ of the input, there is a time $t \le \abs{s} + 1$
such that after $t$ steps from the scan configuration at position $\abs{p}$
with empty output, the marker-existence scanner has halted with output the
single bit recording whether $s$ contains a $1$.
